title.narrative: Two Judges recruited and deployed to try high profile criminal cases

description.narrative: The output will contribute to achieving expeditious and efficient adjudication of criminal cases and reduce backlog in the high court in order to enhance stability in the security sector and contribute to implementation of the nationally agreed reforms. This will be achieved through identification, recruitment and deployment of two (2) independent and impartial foreign judges who will objectively try criminal matters involving high profile former security sector persons accused high crimes. The recruited and deployed judges will be provided with adequate resources necessary for execution of their functions without hinderance.

comment.narrative: End of Project Evaluation. UNDP in consultation with Judiciary the Delegation of European Union the Government and key stakeholders commissioned external end of project evaluation. The end of project evaluation was conducted by an independent consultant whose results were publicly validated by key stakeholders. Based on UNDP and OECD evaluation framework the evaluation assessed the extent to which the Support to Implementation of the Justice Sector Reforms Project had met its objectives to provide evidence of UNDPs contribution towards outcome achievements and role played by and partnerships developed for purposes of informing future programming actions. The specific elements of the evaluation were to a establish to extent to which the planned and related project objectives outcomes and results of the project had been achieved b the relevance efficiency and effectiveness of the project in achieving its objectives outcomes and results c assess factors affecting the project implementation outputs and its sustainability contributing factors and constraints d assess UNDPs strategy used in making contribution to the outcome including use of partnerships for implementation and programming arrangements e examine the extent to which gender and human rights were considered in the projects design implementation and monitoring f establish lessons learnt from project implementation and g make recommendations for improving design effectiveness efficiency and sustainability for future programming.

title.narrative: Impartial, efficient and expeditious disposal of highprofile security related criminal cases for enhance stability in Lesotho

description.narrative: The output will enable SADC, the EU and UNDP supported by local and regional stakeholders make a major contribution to the speedy disposal of highprofile security sector related criminal cases. The output includes provision of highquality prosecution services by the Department of Public Prosecution and efficient adjudication of criminal cases by experienced impartial judges including foreign recruited judges.The output will result in expeditious and efficient adjudication of criminal cases and reduce backlog in the high court in order to enhance stability in the security sector and contribute to implementation of the nationally agreed reforms. The specific activities include:Activity 1.1: Recruitment and deployment of two (2) independent and impartial foreign judges who will objectively try criminal matters involving high profile former security service accused persons;Activity 1.2: Support to trial of criminal cases through case allocation and management system, conduct of the criminal trials, monitoring of trial proceedings to enhance transparency and;Activity 1.3: Technical and operation support to judges, prosecution, investigators, defence lawyers and litigants through provision of logistical support, research and stenographic services.

comment.narrative: Component a of the target Proportion of highprofile security sectorrelated cases investigated and tried was fully achieved when all the cases were investigated and the trial commenced. Component b Proportion of highprofile security sectorrelated casesconcludedresolved was not achieved since none of the cases has been determined. All 8 cases were investigated. Of the 8 ongoing cases the foreign Judge is adjudicating 3 cases and 4 cases were reassigned to local Judges httpssundayexpress.co.lslocaljudgestakeoverhighprofilecases . 1 case was withdrawn and sent back to the magistrates court for an inquest.The ongoing trials have led to the following highimpact progressive qualitative results1.Improved trust and confidence in the Justice system of Lesotho. The End of Project Evaluation concluded that the Project has improved confidence in the Judiciary on delivery of quality justice service and respect for the rule of law. This is also reinforced by improved perception when a trend analysis is conducted for the rating on the Rule of Law indicators in the World Banks Worldwide Governance Indicator for Lesotho 2019 2021 httpinfo.worldbank.orggovernancewgi andAfro Barometer Country Report for Lesotho 2020 2022 httpswww.afrobarometer.org 2.Clear demonstration that no one is above the law and those implicated must be prosecuted. Public perception survey and media reports indicate an improved respect of law as illustrated by reduced instances of abuse of power among highranking officials and leaders. The issuance of warrant of arrest arraignment and enjoining of political leaders including former Deputy Prime Minister and sitting Minister in the HighProfile cases is an attestation attributed to the sustained trial of the criminal cases supported by the Project. httpwww.pcfm.co.lsthehighcourthasissuedawarrantofarrestformerdeputyprimeministerandleaderofthelesothocongressfordemocracymothetjoametsingforfailuretoappearbeforecourttoday httpslestimes.commetsingreturnsfinallyappearsincourt and httpspubliceyenews.commetsingfinallyjoinedinkamolistreasontrial 3.Acquisition and deployment of current reference materials journals law reports and online library subscriptions ensured that the judges have relevant references to ensure impartiality and expedient hearing of the cases httpswww.gov.lsundpeuhandoverofficeequipmenttojudiciarytextUnited20Nations20Development20Program20UNDPthe20Justice20Sector20Reforms20Project. httpswww.africapress.netlesothoallnewseuundpcapacitatehighcourt . 4.Significantly improved stability and reduced conflict in the security sector including security sectorcivilian relations. Evidence from security sector personnel attributes this calm to the ongoing trial httpswww.iol.co.zanewsafricalivefeedsammatekaneofficiallysworninasthe7thprimeministeroflesotho87fd6e94d6e6450797947b910b386dc1 .

title.narrative: Accountable Governance, Effective Institutions, Social Cohesion and Inclusion

description.narrative: The result contributes to achievement of UNDAF Pillar 1 on Accountable Governance, Effective Institutions, Social Cohesion and Inclusion, UNDAF Outcome 1.1 where: By 2023, government and nongovernmental institutions deliver their mandates and uphold good governance, rule of law, and human rights, with all people having improved access to justice and participating in social and political decisionmaking processes in a peaceful environment.This impact result supports implementation of national reforms process that are inclusive, open and participatory.; strengthens the rule of law and human rights institutions to expand access to justice as well as citizen participation and reporting on international instruments and commitments.The project actions contributes to attainment of the impact by supporting the impartial, efficient, and expeditious disposal of highprofile criminal cases for security sector stabilization and strengthening of the justice sector by improving and expanding the availability, accessibility to quality justice service delivery

title.narrative: Effective and efficient project management

description.narrative: UNDP will ensure the project moves towards its goals, implementing activities within time and available resources. This shall be through acquisition and deployment of the necessary tools and resources, generating and managing knowledge, adequate preparation, and installing right personnel. To achieve this, the project is aligned to the global development Agenda 2030, UNDPs global strategic plan, UNDP Regional Bureau for Africas renewed strategic offer in Africa on peace and security, UNDAF outcomes and UNDP CPD outputs. This alignment clearly defines the development challenge to be addressed, making the project management to be precise on what to accomplish. In so doing the stakeholders to be impacted by changes have been defined, the scope of the tasks and resources involved delineated, and the specific objectives the team must fulfil to reach completion determined. The project management will entail development of internal communication strategy to reach out to project partners and effectively communicate results. The Project Management shall also provide policy advise to UNDP the UN and other Development Partners on coordination and consolidation of policy advisory in support of the reforms process. This will be complimented by an external communication strategy to ensure that all stakeholders the EU, Government and other partners are effectively informed, and their inputs sought on a timely basis. Robust tools will be developed to monitor and evaluate project progress. This will include defining project timelines, production of realtime reports on specific activities, drawing on analytics to assess performance and plan future steps and, customizing project workflows for more effective project management. Key activities are: Activity 2.1: Mobilisation and deployment of strategic project personnel and staffing;Activity 2.2: Effective communication, regular monitoring, reporting and evaluation and;Activity 2.4: Operational support to project implementation.

title.narrative: Effective and efficient project management

description.narrative: UNDP will ensure the project moves towards its goals, implementing activities within time and available resources. This shall be through acquisition and deployment of the necessary tools and resources, generating and managing knowledge, adequate preparation, and installing right personnel. To achieve this, the project is aligned to the global development Agenda 2030, UNDPs global strategic plan, UNDP Regional Bureau for Africas renewed strategic offer in Africa on peace and security, UNDAF outcomes and UNDP CPD outputs. This alignment clearly defines the development challenge to be addressed, making the project management to be precise on what to accomplish. In so doing the stakeholders to be impacted by changes have been defined, the scope of the tasks and resources involved delineated, and the specific objectives the team must fulfil to reach completion determined. The project management will entail development of internal communication strategy to reach out to project partners and effectively communicate results. The Project Management shall also provide policy advise to UNDP the UN and other Development Partners on coordination and consolidation of policy advisory in support of the reforms process. This will be complimented by an external communication strategy to ensure that all stakeholders the EU, Government and other partners are effectively informed, and their inputs sought on a timely basis. Robust tools will be developed to monitor and evaluate project progress. This will include defining project timelines, production of realtime reports on specific activities, drawing on analytics to assess performance and plan future steps and, customizing project workflows for more effective project management. Key activities are: Activity 2.1: Mobilisation and deployment of strategic project personnel and staffing;Activity 2.2: Effective communication, regular monitoring, reporting and evaluation and;Activity 2.4: Operational support to project implementation.
